$comment: Known folders and files. Paths use tokens: {windir} {programfiles} {programfilesx86} {programdata} {systemdrive} {users} (the folder holding all user profiles) and {anydrive} (any drive letter). '*' matches one folder name (or a name pattern), '**' matches any number of folders. A rule applies to the matched item and, unless something more specific matches, everything inside it. 'owner' is shown as 'Belongs to' when no installed program claims the item. 'protect' marks what must be kept: system = Windows needs it (never delete), program = installed software (uninstall instead), caution = deleting has side effects (cloud sync, browser profiles, saves, VM disks). Rules without it give no protection of their own. 'advice' says what to do with the contents: recommend/safe/review = can be deleted once older than minAgeDays (deleteFolder: the folder itself can go too), keep = leave it, tool = use the named Windows tool, inapp = remove it from the app that manages it.

rules.name: Windows
rules.description: The Windows operating system. Windows needs these files to start and run.

rules.name: Windows system files
rules.description: Core Windows programs and components (SysWOW64 holds the 32-bit versions). Never delete files here by hand.

rules.name: Windows drivers
rules.description: Drivers that let Windows use your hardware. Removing them can stop devices or Windows from working.

rules.name: Driver store
rules.description: Windows' library of installed driver packages. Old driver versions can be removed safely only through Windows tools (for example Disk Cleanup or pnputil), never by deleting files.

rules.name: Windows component store (WinSxS)
rules.description: Windows keeps every system component and its versions here. Much of its apparent size is shared with System32 (the same files counted twice). Clean it only with Disk Cleanup or 'DISM /Cleanup-Image'.

rules.name: Windows Installer cache
rules.description: Copies of installer packages that programs need for repair, update and uninstall. Deleting them by hand can make programs impossible to update or remove.

rules.name: Windows Installer patch cache
rules.description: Baseline files used when patching installed programs. Can be large; only remove with official tools.

rules.name: Windows Update working folder
rules.description: Where Windows Update keeps its database and downloads.

rules.name: Windows Update downloads
rules.description: Update files already downloaded. Once updates are installed these are not needed; Disk Cleanup removes them safely.

advice.why: Update files Windows already installed.
advice.tool: Disk Cleanup > Clean up system files > Windows Update Cleanup

rules.name: Delivery Optimization cache
rules.description: Update pieces Windows keeps to share with other PCs. Safe to clear with Disk Cleanup.

advice.why: Update pieces kept to share with other PCs.

rules.name: Windows temporary files
rules.description: Temporary files created by Windows and installers. Old files here are normally safe to remove.

advice.why: Temporary files programs and installers left behind. Windows and programs don't need them once they're a few days old.

rules.name: Windows logs
rules.description: Diagnostic logs Windows writes. Useful for troubleshooting; old logs are usually not needed.

advice.why: Diagnostic logs. Old ones are only useful for troubleshooting past problems.

rules.name: Windows crash dumps
rules.description: Snapshots saved when Windows crashed (blue screens) or a driver hung. Only useful to diagnose those crashes.

advice.why: Crash reports only help diagnose crashes that already happened.

rules.name: Full Windows crash dump
rules.description: Full memory snapshot from the last Windows crash. Often very large; only useful for diagnosing that crash.

advice.why: Crash reports only help diagnose crashes that already happened.

rules.name: Prefetch
rules.description: Windows' record of how programs start, used to launch them faster. Small; deleting it slows startup temporarily and loses usage history.

advice.why: Small files Windows uses to start programs faster; Windows manages them itself.

rules.name: Installed fonts
rules.description: Fonts available to all programs.

rules.name: .NET Framework global assembly cache
rules.description: Shared .NET Framework components used by many programs.

rules.name: Windows servicing
rules.description: Files Windows uses to install updates and features.

rules.name: Built-in Windows apps
rules.description: Apps that are part of Windows (Start menu, Settings, …).

rules.name: Driver setup information
rules.description: Descriptions Windows uses to install drivers.

rules.name: Offline files cache
rules.description: Offline copies of network files. Managed by the Sync Center.

rules.name: Previous Windows installation
rules.description: Your previous version of Windows, kept after an upgrade so you can go back. Windows removes it automatically after about 10 days; Disk Cleanup ('Previous Windows installations') removes it safely.

advice.why: Your previous Windows, kept only so you can go back after an upgrade.
advice.tool: Disk Cleanup > Clean up system files > Previous Windows installation(s)

rules.name: Windows upgrade files
rules.description: Temporary files from a Windows upgrade or reset. Not needed once the upgrade is finished; Disk Cleanup removes them.

advice.why: Leftovers from a finished Windows upgrade.
advice.tool: Disk Cleanup > Clean up system files > Temporary Windows installation files
